facts.heading: GP suggested therapy visit
facts.content: Daniel's GP suggested he come to therapy because she observed he looked exhausted.
facts.evidence: My GP suggested I come. She said I look exhausted, and she's right, I am.

facts.heading: Burnout started in October
facts.content: Daniel has been completely burned out since October.
facts.evidence: I've been completely burned out since October.

facts.heading: Workload increased after client loss
facts.content: Daniel's company lost a big client, and he ended up doing three people's jobs.
facts.evidence: We lost a big client, and half the team got moved onto the rescue plan, so I ended up doing three people's jobs.

facts.heading: Works long hours
facts.content: Daniel starts work at seven and continues answering messages until ten at night.
facts.evidence: I'm at my desk by seven and I'm still answering messages at ten at night.

facts.heading: Sleep is poor

facts.evidence: Most nights I sleep about four hours.

facts.heading: Wakes at three AM

facts.evidence: I wake up at three in the morning and can't fall back asleep.

facts.heading: Dreading nights

facts.evidence: I've started dreading the nights, if I'm honest.

facts.heading: Father diagnosed with Parkinson's
facts.content: Daniel's father was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.
facts.evidence: My father. He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.

facts.heading: Father's condition details

facts.evidence: His hands shake, and he's slower, and he gets frustrated.

facts.heading: Daniel drives father to hospital
facts.content: Daniel drives his father to the hospital in Leeds for neurology appointments every few weeks.
facts.evidence: I'm the one who drives him to the hospital in Leeds. The neurology appointments are every few weeks, and it's an hour each way.

facts.heading: Hannah lives in Toronto
facts.content: Daniel's younger sister, Hannah, lives in Toronto.
facts.evidence: My younger sister Hannah lives in Toronto, so all the care for our father falls on me.

facts.heading: Feels guilty about being tired
facts.content: Daniel feels it is selfish to be tired when his father is ill.
facts.evidence: I feel it's selfish to be tired when he's the one who's ill.

facts.heading: Tells sister he is fine
facts.content: When his sister asks how he is, Daniel tells her he is fine.
facts.evidence: She asks how I am and I say fine.

facts.heading: Cannot face hospital visits
facts.content: Some days Daniel sits in the hospital car park for ten minutes before going in.
facts.evidence: That some days I sit in the car park at the hospital for ten minutes before I go in, because I can't face it.

facts.heading: GP found tests normal

facts.evidence: She did blood tests, and they were all normal

facts.heading: GP attributed issues to stress

facts.evidence: She said it's stress and exhaustion

facts.evidence: She's very patient. She makes me tea and doesn't push me to talk

facts.heading: Work emails prevent travel
facts.content: Daniel feels he cannot go away because of emails and his dad.
facts.evidence: The emails. If I'm away I'll come back to two hundred of them. And Dad might need something.

facts.heading: Daniel stopped running two months ago
facts.content: Daniel stopped running about two months ago.
facts.evidence: I stopped about two months ago

facts.heading: Daniel ran six years
facts.content: Daniel ran ten kilometres every Saturday morning for six years.
facts.evidence: I ran. Ten kilometres every Saturday morning. I'd done it for six years.

facts.heading: Running was a personal time
facts.content: Daniel felt running was the one time in the week nobody could reach him.
facts.evidence: It was the one time in the week nobody could reach me

facts.heading: Boss sends late emails
facts.content: Daniel's boss, Peterson, sends emails at eleven at night.
facts.evidence: he sends emails at eleven at night

facts.heading: Boss expects early replies
facts.content: Daniel's boss expects an answer to emails before breakfast.
facts.evidence: and expects an answer before breakfast

facts.heading: Daniel answers all boss emails
facts.content: Daniel answers every email from his boss.
facts.evidence: I answer it. Every time

facts.heading: Daniel fears job loss
facts.content: Daniel is afraid his boss will think he isn't committed.
facts.evidence: That he'd think I wasn't committed

facts.heading: Restructuring planned in spring
facts.content: There is a restructuring planned in the spring.
facts.evidence: There's a restructuring in the spring

facts.heading: Daniel has a mortgage
facts.content: Daniel has a mortgage.
facts.evidence: I have a mortgage

facts.heading: Daniel feels flat and irritable
facts.content: Daniel reports feeling flat and irritable.
facts.evidence: Flat, mostly. And irritable

facts.heading: Daniel experienced physical symptoms
facts.content: Daniel felt his heart racing and hands shaking in the toilets.
facts.evidence: My heart was going and my hands were shaking

facts.heading: Past panic attacks experienced
facts.content: Daniel has experienced episodes like this a couple of times.
facts.evidence: A couple of times

facts.heading: Panic attack on train to Manchester
facts.content: Daniel had an episode on the train to Manchester where he had to get off and stand on the platform.
facts.evidence: Once on the train to Manchester. I just had to get off and stand on the platform.

facts.heading: Fear of losing control
facts.content: Daniel fears that he is losing his mind and is not coping.
facts.evidence: That I'm losing it. That I'm going to end up like, I don't know. Not coping.

facts.heading: Coping with anxiety via coffee
facts.content: Daniel drinks about six cups of coffee per day.
facts.evidence: I'm on about six cups a day.

facts.heading: Using wine to switch off
facts.content: Daniel has started drinking wine in the evenings, consuming two or three glasses.
facts.evidence: I've started having wine in the evenings to switch my head off. Two glasses, sometimes three.

facts.heading: Wine does not improve sleep
facts.content: Daniel feels uneasy about the wine, and it only works for an hour before he wakes up at three.
facts.evidence: Uneasy. It works for an hour and then I wake at three anyway.

facts.heading: Relief from sharing burdens
facts.content: Daniel felt a sense of relief after sharing his burdens with the therapist.
facts.evidence: A bit of a relief, actually. Like putting down a bag I didn't realise I was carrying.

facts.heading: Sleep is primary coping need

facts.evidence: If I could sleep I could probably cope with the rest.

facts.heading: Family history of stoicism
facts.content: Daniel's grandfather worked in the mines in Yorkshire and never complained.
facts.evidence: My grandfather worked in the mines in Yorkshire. He never complained about anything, not once.

facts.heading: Fear of disappointing grandfather

facts.evidence: I keep thinking he would think I was weak for being here.

facts.evidence: Yes. Half past nine, perhaps. I could make it a thing with Claire. Tea on the sofa.

facts.evidence: I'll write down when I wake up, if I wake up.
